newsitem.title: JAPAN: Private body should keep Japan nuclear waste-panel.
newsitem.headline: Private body should keep Japan nuclear waste-panel.

text.p: A government advisory panel on nuclear waste said that high-level radioactive waste would best be taken care of by a private entity led by the electric power utilities which generate the waste.

The panel under the Atomic Energy Commission said industrial waste should be taken care of by the producer and that therefore a private entity led by electric power firms should, under government supervison, be responsible for the storage of high-level nuclear waste.
The government has already said it plans to set up a new entity by 2000 which would be in charge of selecting and managing permanent nuclear waste storage sites.

However, the electricity industry has insisted that long-term, large-scale projects such as nuclear waste storage were not suited for private enterprise and could only be carried out by government-led bodies.
Currently, Japan's high-level nuclear waste is sent to a temporary site in Rokkashomura in Aomori prefecture, northern Japan, to store for 30 to 50 years until it cools down.
High-level nuclear waste, sealed in stainless steel canisters, has started to accumulate in the Rokkashomura facility, but a permanent storage site has yet to be decided.

The draft recommendations by the panel, issued on Thursday, also said the costs of the nuclear waste disposal should be passed on to electricity rates and be shouldered by end-users, which some industry analysts say runs counter to recent government calls to slash rates.
A Science and Technology Agency official, which oversees the technical aspects of nuclear power, said the panel would come up with a final proposal by next spring.
